summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Old Trafford commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 369/10 (111.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 197/10 (64.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Chris Woakes (6/50), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Stuart Broad delivered a masterclass for England (62 Runs & 10 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 48%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by Rory Burns (147 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by 269 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
